name: Lovefield
tagline: Google's pure-JavaScript relational database for web apps, layered over IndexedDB; archived since 2021.
description: Lovefield is a relational query engine written in JavaScript by Google and open-sourced in 2014-2015. You declare a typed schema, and a fluent SQL-like API (select, from, where, innerJoin, orderBy, groupBy) runs queries with an optimizer, indexes, constraints, transactions and observable queries for data binding, persisting rows to IndexedDB or keeping them in memory (Firebase was an optional backend). It worked across Chrome, Firefox, IE 11, Edge and Safari and, per its FAQ, Inbox by Gmail relied on it heavily. The last npm release, 2.1.12, dates from February 2017 and the GitHub repository is archived; for new browser apps, SQLite compiled to WebAssembly, PGlite or Dexie are the usual choices.
statusNote: GitHub repository archived (no commits since Aug 2021); last npm release 2.1.12 (Feb 2017). Consider SQLite WASM, PGlite or Dexie.

scale.notes: Bounded by browser storage quotas and memory.

strengths: Real relational queries with joins, aggregation and an optimizer in the browser
Declarative schema with indexes, constraints and transactions
Observable queries for UI data binding
Proven at scale inside Inbox by Gmail
weaknesses: Fluent API rather than SQL text; no SQL compatibility
Performance bounded by IndexedDB and JavaScript execution
useCases: Maintaining older web apps built on it
Learning how a relational engine maps onto IndexedDB
notIdealFor: New browser apps (prefer SQLite WASM, PGlite or Dexie)
